facts.label: official
facts.quote: The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 3.75% to 4%, which was raised to this level on 16 September this year, marking the first US Fed interest rate hike since 2023.
facts.text: The US Federal Reserve held the benchmark federal funds rate steady in the target range of 3.75% to 4.00%.

facts.label: official
facts.quote: The FOMC approved the policy decision by a 10 – 2 vote, with Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack dissenting in favour of a 25-basis-point rate hike.
facts.text: The Federal Open Market Committee decided by a 10 to 2 vote to maintain the interest rate target unchanged.

facts.label: official
facts.quote: Two members wanted to raise it by 25 basis points.
facts.text: Two dissenting policymakers voted in favor of hiking the policy rate by 25 basis points.

facts.label: official
facts.quote: The accumulation of more information will help the Committee determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the Committee's 2% goal.
facts.text: The Federal Reserve reiterated its policy objective to return annual inflation to 2%.

facts.label: reported
facts.quote: Inflation in September saw significant uptick as consumer prices rose 3.7% compared with a year earlier.
facts.text: US headline consumer price inflation increased to 3.7% year-on-year in September.

facts.label: reported
facts.quote: Core CPI, which excludes volatile food and energy prices, stood at 2.6%, up 0.3 percentage point from August.
facts.text: US core consumer inflation excluding food and energy climbed to 2.6% in September.

facts.label: analyst-view
facts.quote: Financial markets are pricing in an 87.4% likelihood of a 25-basis-point rate hike at the Fed's next meeting in December, up from 78.3% on Tuesday, according to CME's FedWatch tool.
facts.text: Financial markets priced in an 87.4% chance of a 25-basis-point interest rate increase at the December FOMC meeting.

facts.label: reported
facts.quote: Two-year yields, which are more sensitive to the Fed's policy path, fell as much as four basis points to 4.7% on Wednesday after Warsh's remarks.
facts.text: US two-year Treasury yields fell to 4.7% following policy statements from the central bank.

facts.label: analyst-view
facts.quote: Experts say the decision was already priced in, while crude oil near $115 a barrel, rising US bond yields, rupee weakness and foreign investor selling remain bigger risks.
facts.text: Crude oil trading near 115 USD per barrel remains a significant risk factor for domestic fuel prices and imported inflation in India.

facts.label: reported
facts.quote: At the same time, the housing market is struggling under the pressure of mortgage rates above 7%.
facts.text: Persistent interest rate pressures have kept benchmark home mortgage rates above 7%, restraining housing affordability and increasing loan burdens.

scenes.vo: America ne byaaj nahi badhaya, phir aapki EMI kyun nahi ghat rahi?

scenes.label: setup

visual.prompt: Inside a large wood-panelled meeting room, a long table with unnamed officials in suits, one lowering a gavel gently, calm serious mood, daylight through tall windows, no text

scenes.vo: US Fed ne pichle hafte rate wahi rakha, lagbhag 4 percent. Fed yaani America ka RBI, jo wahan byaaj tay karta hai.

scenes.label: setup

scenes.vo: Yeh khabar TV pe aayi, toh ghar mein sabne rahat ki saans li. Sabko laga, ab loan sasta hoga.

scenes.vo: Soch simple thi, America ne rate nahi badhaya, toh RBI ab ghatayega. RBI ghatayega, toh bank bhi home loan ka byaaj kam karega.
